{"id":"5976ec62-ea13-4774-ba5e-a1f34751e09c","object":"chat.completion","created":1790493322,"model":"deepseek-flash","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"{"requirements":[{"requirement":"A musical artist's first name matches part of the name of a charity."},{"requirement":"The charity is unrelated to the musical artist and was registered between 2000 and 2010 inclusive."},{"requirement":"The musical artist died in a city."},{"requirement":"The city where the musical artist died is in a country, and that city is 20 to 30 miles inclusive from the site of that country's deadliest aviation accident as of 2023."},{"requirement":"The aviation accident occurred 15 years prior to the musical artist's accidental death."},{"requirement":"The musical artist had a partner at the time of the musical artist's death."},{"requirement":"That partner gave an interview in which the partner said that following the musical artist's death, the musical artist has become a direct reference to one of the musical artist's songs."},{"requirement":"The title of the song referenced in the partner's statement is one word and an adjective."},{"requirement":"The requested song title is the title of that song."}]}","reasoning_content":"We need answer only JSON object with requirements. Need decompose question into candidate requirements. Need preserve semantics. We need not solve. We need identify requirements: entities/relations. Original question: musical artist shares first name with part of charity's name. Charity unrelated, registered 2000-2010 inclusive. Artist died in a city that is 20-30 miles from site of that country's deadliest aviation accident as of 2023. Aviation accident occurred 15 years prior to artist's accidental death. Partner of artist at time of death gave interview where said following their death, artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs. Song title one word adjective. Ask song title.

Need candidate requirements. Should include intermediate identification/existence. Need preserve role identity uncertainty: "the partner" and "artist" etc. The artist died accidental; partner at time of death. "their" ambiguous? "following their death" likely artist's death; partner gave interview. We must not assume partner gender. "their songs" could artist's songs? "one of their songs" likely artist's songs. Need preserve.

We need produce small set coherent candidate requirements. Could be around 6-10. They said each requirement one coherent object/event/relation/attribute. Avoid combining independent requirements. But can keep complementary conditions together when jointly identify same object.

Let's list possible requirements:

1. Identify a musical artist whose first name matches part of the name of a charity. This relation: artist's first name is shared with part of charity's name. This may require both artist and charity. "shares their first name with part of a charity's name." It identifies relation between artist first name and a substring/part of charity name. Could combine with charity unrelated and registered period? Maybe separate charity properties.

2. Identify the charity: unrelated to the musical artist, registered between 2000 and 2010 inclusive. This is coherent object with attributes. But requirement 1 already links artist and charity. Could separate: "There exists a charity whose name includes a part equal to the musical artist's first name; the charity is unrelated to the artist and was registered between 2000 and 2010 inclusive." That combines relation and attributes of same charity. But maybe Q1/Q2 are two addressable units. The instruction says do not combine independent requirements merely because they contribute. But here Q1 relation and Q2 attributes both concern same charity. Could keep as one? But Q2 includes unrelated and registered period. It's coherent about charity. Q1 is relation. I'd separate relation from charity attributes? Hmm.

3. The artist died in a city. Need identify city.

4. The city is 20-30 miles inclusive away from the site of that country's deadliest aviation accident as of 2023. "that country" refers to country? Which country? likely country of the city? The city is in a country; that country's deadliest aviation accident. Need preserve. Requirement: The city where artist died is located 20-30 miles from the site of the deadliest aviation accident in that country as of 2023. Need also identify the country and accident site. Could be one requirement about distance and site.

5. The aviation accident occurred 15 years prior to artist's accidental death. Need relation between accident date and death date. Also artist's death was accidental. Need perhaps separate: artist's death was accidental; accident occurred 15 years before death. Q4 includes both. "The aviation accident occurred 15 years prior to the artist’s accidental death." So requirement: The artist's death was accidental and occurred 15 years after the aviation accident. Temporal attachment.

6. Partner of artist at time of death gave an interview. Need identify partner and interview. Requirement: The artist had a partner at the time of the artist's death; that partner gave an interview.

7. In the interview, the partner said that following the artist's death, the artist has become a direct reference to one of the artist's songs. Need statement relation. Preserve "their" maybe artist's songs? The phrase: "the artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs" Ambiguous: "their" could refer to artist? Since artist has songs. Could be partner? But likely artist's songs. Need not resolve? We can phrase "one of the songs of the artist (or the relevant person as described in the question)"? Hmm. The question says "one of their songs" with "the artist" as antecedent? Actually "the artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs." Grammatically "their" can refer to artist? The artist became a direct reference to one of their songs. Yes. We can say "one of the artist's songs." But role identity uncertainty? It is clear? The artist is musical artist. We'll preserve as "one of the musical artist's songs" because "their" likely artist. But if strict, "their" could refer to partner? The partner said "following their death, the artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs." The first their = artist's death, second their = artist's. So okay.

8. The song title is one word and an adjective. Need requested attribute: the title of that song. Requirement: The song's title is a one-word adjective. And final: What is the title? Could include "Identify the title of the song." But requirement should state what must be established: The title of the song identified by the partner's statement is a one-word adjective. The final answer is that title. We can include "The requested output is the title of that song." But schema wants requirements. We can include "The title of the song ...".

Need maybe intermediate identification of "country" and "deadliest aviation accident as of 2023". The city is 20-30 miles from site of that country's deadliest aviation accident. Need identify country from city? The city is in a country. Need requirement: There is a country whose deadliest aviation accident as of 2023 occurred at a site 20-30 miles from the city where the artist died. This includes country. Could phrase.

Need "as of 2023" temporal attachment to deadliest aviation accident. Must preserve.

Need "registered between 2000 and 2010 inclusive" attached to charity.

Need "unrelated to musical artist" attached to charity. Could be separate from registration? It's attribute. Could combine with charity registration.

Need "partner at time of death" attached to partner. "at the time of their death" modifies partner. Preserve temporal attachment: partner of artist at the time of artist's death. Could be one requirement.

Need "gave an interview where they said..." This is relation: partner gave interview; in interview partner said statement. Could combine with statement? It's same event. It says "partner ... gave an interview where they said that..." So one coherent event: interview and its content. Maybe include both.

Need "following their death" = after artist's death. The artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs. Could phrase.

Need "direct reference" maybe preserve exact wording. It says "the artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs." We should preserve "direct reference" maybe.

Need "accidental death" attached to artist. Q4 says "artist's accidental death" and Q3 says "This musical artist died in a city". Q5 "at time of their death". Need maybe requirement that artist's death was accidental. This is important because Q4 uses "accidental death". We can include in Q4 requirement.

Potential final requirements:

1. A musical artist's first name is shared with part of the name of a charity. (Relation)
2. The charity is unrelated to the musical artist and was registered between 2000 and 2010 inclusive. (Charity attributes)
3. The musical artist died in a city. (Death place)
4. The city where the musical artist died is 20 to 30 miles inclusive from the site of the deadliest aviation accident in that country as of 2023. (Distance and accident site)
5. The aviation accident occurred 15 years prior to the musical artist's accidental death. (Temporal relation and accidental death)
6. The musical artist had a partner at the time of the artist's death. (Partner relation)
7. That partner gave an interview in which the partner said that following the artist's death, the artist has become a direct reference to one of the artist's songs. (Interview and statement)
8. The title of the song referenced by the partner's statement is a one-word adjective. (Song title attribute)
9. What is the title of that song? Maybe requirement: The requested attribute is the title of that song. But question asks. Could include "The answer sought is the title of that song." But maybe not a requirement. The instruction: represent what must eventually be established to answer. So include requested attribute: "The title of the song is to be identified." But Q7 is the question. We can include as requirement "Identify the title of the song that satisfies all above." But maybe redundant. They ask return requirements. We can include final requested attribute: "The requested output is the title of the song that is a one-word adjective and is referenced in the partner's statement." But Q8 already. Hmm.

Need maybe "site of that country's deadliest aviation accident" depends on identifying the country. Should we include requirement to identify the country? The city where artist died belongs to a country. The country's deadliest aviation accident. So requirement: "The country in which the city of the artist's death is located has a deadliest aviation accident as of 2023; the site of that accident is 20-30 miles from the city." That combines country and site. But maybe separate: "Identify the country in which the city of the artist's death is located." But that's intermediate. The original doesn't explicitly ask for country, but relation uses "that country". Since "that country" refers to country of death city. We should preserve. Could make a requirement: "The city where the artist died is in a country." But trivial. The distance relation to that country's deadliest aviation accident. So one requirement can include "that country" and accident. It implies country. That's okay.

Need "as of 2023" attached to deadliest aviation accident. Include.

Need "accident occurred 15 years prior to artist's accidental death" means accident date = death date - 15 years. Also artist's death accidental. Include.

Need "charity unrelated to artist" maybe "unrelated" could mean no connection. Preserve exact.

Need "shares their first name with part of a charity's name" — "part of a charity's name" could be a word in charity name. We can phrase "part of the charity's name matches the musical artist's first name." Good.

Need role identity uncertainty: "the partner" is one person? We don't know if partner same as any other role. No overlap with others. "the artist" and "musical artist" same. The question does establish "This musical artist" same as Q1 artist? Yes Q1 "A musical artist", Q3 "This musical artist" refers same. Q4 "the artist's" same. Q5 "the artist" same. So can say the musical artist throughout. That's fine. "partner of the artist" distinct role, not to assume different from others? Not relevant. But preserve not assume partner equals something. No issue.

Need maybe "at the time of their death" modifies partner. So "partner of the artist at the time of the artist's death." Good.

Need "one of their songs" — we should preserve "one of their songs" not change which entity? Could phrase "one of the musical artist's songs" but is that changing? The pronoun "their" likely refers to artist. But to preserve role identity uncertainty, maybe keep "one of their songs" with antecedent? Hmm. The original says "the artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs." The "their" could refer to artist. We can write "one of the musical artist's songs" as interpretation. But if strict, maybe "one of the songs of the person referred to as 'their' in the question" but that's awkward. The question says musical artist. The partner said "the artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs." The artist is the one who has songs. So okay.

Need maybe "direct reference" exact. Good.

Now output JSON only. Ensure valid JSON. No extra text. We'll produce around 8 requirements.

Could we combine 1 and 2? The instructions: "Do not combine independent requirements merely because they contribute to the same final answer." Q1 and Q2 both about charity relation. They are independent? Q1 identifies relation between artist and charity; Q2 gives charity attributes. They are separate facts. Could be separate. Keep separate.

Could combine Q3 and Q4? Q3 artist died in a city. Q4 aviation accident 15 years prior to artist's accidental death. Q3 and Q4 both death. But Q3 is location, Q4 is temporal relation. Keep separate.

Could combine Q4 and artist's accidental death? Q4 includes "artist's accidental death". So requirement: "The musical artist's death was accidental and occurred 15 years after the aviation accident." That's one coherent temporal relation plus death manner. Could separate accidental death from temporal relation? The date relation uses death. But combined is fine because they jointly specify the death event. However, "accidental death" is an attribute of death event. "aviation accident occurred 15 years prior" is relation between two events. Could combine as one requirement about the death event and temporal relation. That's okay.

Could combine Q5 and Q6? Q5 partner interview and statement; Q6 song title one-word adjective. Separate: song title attribute. Q6 is about song. Q5 references song. Keep separate.

Could include final requested attribute: "The answer sought is the title of the song identified in the partner's statement." But Q8 says title is one-word adjective. The final question asks what is the song title. Requirement 9 could be "The title of that song is to be determined." But requirements are what must be established. Q8 establishes it's one-word adjective, but not the actual title. The final answer is the title. So maybe include "The song title itself is the requested attribute." The schema wants requirements. Could include "The title of the song referenced in the partner's statement is the requested information." But that's meta. The instruction says represent what must eventually be established. So final requirement could be "The title of the song is [unknown]". But candidate requirements should be objects/events/relations/requested attributes. The requested attribute is the song title. So include "The requested attribute is the title of the song." However, Q6 already says title is one-word adjective. The answer seeks the actual title. I think include: "The title of the song is the requested attribute." But that may be too meta. Let's see examples? No examples. We can include "The title of the song is to be identified." But schema says requirement. I'll include as requirement 9: "The title of the song that satisfies the above is the requested answer." But maybe not necessary. The final question is already the overall objective. The candidate requirements should preserve question meaning, including Q7. So yes include.

Need ensure no outside knowledge. We're not using any.

Let's draft JSON:

{
  "requirements": [
    {"requirement": "A musical artist's first name matches part of the name of a charity."},
    {"requirement": "The charity is unrelated to the musical artist and was registered between 2000 and 2010 inclusive."},
    {"requirement": "The musical artist died in a city."},
    {"requirement": "The city where the musical artist died is 20 to 30 miles inclusive from the site of the deadliest aviation accident in that country as of 2023."},
    {"requirement": "The aviation accident occurred 15 years prior to the musical artist's accidental death."},
    {"requirement": "The musical artist had a partner at the time of the musical artist's death."},
    {"requirement": "That partner gave an interview in which the partner said that following the musical artist's death, the musical artist has become a direct reference to one of the musical artist's songs."},
    {"requirement": "The title of the song referenced in the partner's statement is one word and an adjective."},
    {"requirement": "The requested song title is the title of that song."}
  ]
}

Check requirement 4: "that country" — but we haven't introduced country. The original says "that country's deadliest aviation accident". The country is presumably the country of the city? We need make clear. We can phrase "The city where the musical artist died is in a country; the city is 20 to 30 miles inclusive from the site of that country's deadliest aviation accident as of 2023." That includes country. Better.

Requirement 5: "The aviation accident occurred 15 years prior to the musical artist's accidental death." This uses the aviation accident from req 4. Good.

Requirement 6: "The musical artist had a partner at the time of the musical artist's death." That preserves temporal. Could be "The partner of the musical artist at the time of the musical artist's death." Good.

Requirement 7: "That partner gave an interview..." "That partner" refers to req 6. Good. "following the musical artist's death, the musical artist has become a direct reference to one of the musical artist's songs." Preserves quote? "has become" present perfect. Good. "direct reference" exact.

Requirement 8: "The title of the song referenced in the partner's statement is one word and an adjective." This combines one word and adjective. Good.

Requirement 9: "The requested song title is the title of that song." Maybe redundant. Could omit? The original question asks "What is the song title?" The final requirement can be "Identify the title of that song." But if we include, it's the requested attribute. The instruction says include necessary intermediate identification/existence objectives when final requested attribute depends on entity... Here final requested attribute is song title. Requirement 8 says title is one-word adjective. Requirement 9 says the requested attribute is the title. That seems fine.

But maybe they want only requirements, not meta. Could phrase: "The title of the song, which is a one-word adjective, is the information sought." But that's meta. Alternatively, "The title of the song is to be identified." That's okay.

Could we combine Q6 and Q7? Q7 is about song reference, Q6 about title attribute. They are separate facts about same song. Could combine: "The partner's statement refers to one of the artist's songs whose title is a one-word adjective." But then we lose the interview event? Actually Q7 includes interview and statement. We can combine song reference and title attribute into one requirement about the song: "The song to which the partner said the artist has become a direct reference is one of the artist's songs and has a one-word adjective title." But that combines independent requirements? The title attribute and the reference are about same song, but they are different facts. The instruction says don't combine independent requirements merely because they contribute to same final answer. They are about same song, but Q7 identifies song via reference, Q6 identifies title property. Could keep separate.

Need maybe "charity's name" part. "shares their first name with part of a charity’s name" could mean the artist's first name is a part of the charity's name. We wrote matches part. Good.

Potential issue: "The charity is unrelated to the musical artist" — we preserved. "registered between 2000 and 2010 inclusive" — yes.

Potential issue: "deadliest aviation accident (as of 2023)" — our requirement says "deadliest aviation accident in that country as of 2023." Good.

Potential issue: "accident occurred 15 years prior to the artist's accidental death" — our requirement says "The aviation accident occurred 15 years prior to the musical artist's accidental death." It doesn't explicitly say artist's death was accidental? It says "accidental death". That implies. Good.

Potential issue: "The partner of the artist (at the time of their death) gave an interview where they said..." Our requirement 6 and 7. Good.

Potential issue: "one of their songs" — we wrote "one of the musical artist's songs." Should we preserve pronoun ambiguity? The instruction says preserve role identity uncertainty. The "their" could refer to artist or partner? Let's parse: "The partner of the artist (at the time of their death) gave an interview where they said that following their death, the artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs." The first "their death" likely artist's death. Second "their" in "following their death" also artist's death. Third "their songs" likely artist's songs. So no uncertainty. We can say artist's songs. Good.

Potential issue: "The title of the song is one word, an adjective." We wrote one word and an adjective. Good.
